hero.title: Specify first. The AI builds what was decided.
hero.subtitle: Open source skill kit for AI coding assistants. It guides the work through SDD (Spec-Driven Development): the request becomes documentation — architecture, requirements, plan — before it becomes code.

lines.text: This request is: A · B · C · D

loose.label: Loose request
results: Token in the URL, written to the server log
Message that reveals whether the e-mail is registered

spec.label: Specification
rules: RN-03: same response whether the e-mail exists or not
spec.result: Single-use link, valid for 30 minutes, with a neutral response.

cards.title: Documentation before code
cards.text: Every request goes through architecture, requirements, interface and plan before the first line of code. The AI receives decisions, not a loose request.

cards.title: End-to-end traceability
cards.text: Decisions, rules, scenarios, screens, tasks, reviews and tests link by IDs. You can follow a rule all the way to the test that guarantees it.

cards.title: The developer in control
cards.text: You approve every phase, decide the estimates and validate the deliveries. The AI suggests; you decide.

whatIs.academic: College project, open source, MIT licensed.
whatIs.language: The kit skills and artifacts are in Portuguese by default. With project.language: en in docs/sdd/config.yml, artifacts are generated in English — which is how the document excerpts on this page are shown.

groups.title: Quality
items: AI without context improvises. With the specification ready, it builds what was decided.
Review applies the same criteria to human and AI code — and includes security.
Traceability shows what is missing: a rule without a test, a task without a review.

groups.title: Control
items: Every decision is recorded with its reason.
One task at a time means small changes, easy to review and to undo.
You approve every phase, decide the estimates and validate the deliveries.

groups.title: Portability
items: No lock-in to one AI: AGENTS.md is the shared context that Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others read.
Stack profiles: full Rails (6.1 → 8.x); Node.js/TypeScript, Python, .NET, Go, Java/Kotlin and PHP with profile and permissions; generic profile for the rest.

pipeline.intro: Pick a request and scroll: each phase shows the command, the input, the generated document and the IDs it creates — and each ID links to its parent ID.

loop.title: Execution ⇄ Review
loop.intro: One task at a time: each one is executed, reviewed and only then closed. A blocking finding sends the task back once before it closes.
loop.label: Plan tasks

trace.intro: Each rule becomes a scenario, screen, task, review and test — always with the same ID. Focus an ID to see what links to it. The example is the password recovery demand.
trace.matrixCaption: Traceability matrix for password recovery: rule, scenarios, screens, tasks and tests

commands.intro: Names are the same in every language. In Claude Code, call them with a slash; in Codex, with a dollar sign. Hover or focus a command to preview what it delivers.

groupNotes.fases: One at a time, in pipeline order. The prototype is optional.
groupNotes.navegacao: They tell you where you are and what is missing.
groupNotes.apoio: Outside the phase loop, when you need them.

sdd-architect.generates: Architecture proposal, one ADR per decision and C4 diagrams
preview: C4 context and container diagrams in Mermaid

sdd-prd.when: A demand needs to become requirements
sdd-prd.generates: PRD with RN-XX rules and CA-XX Gherkin scenarios

sdd-prototype.when: The PRD has an interface (optional phase)
sdd-prototype.generates: SPEC-UI with the UI-XX screens and their states

sdd-plan.generates: Plan with small, testable T-XX tasks
preview: T-01 … T-05 · each implements RN and validates CA

sdd-execute.when: Implement one task from the plan
sdd-execute.generates: Code and tests for a single T-XX
preview: T-03 — Validate token and change password

sdd-review.generates: REVIEW-T-XX with R-XX findings by severity

sdd-start.generates: Asks for the entry point and calls the right phase
preview: A — new system: architecture, then PRD
B — feature in an existing system: PRD
C — I already have the PRD: plan

sdd-next.when: Not sure what to do now
sdd-next.generates: Where the pipeline stands and the next action

sdd-trace.generates: RN → CA → UI → T → test matrix, with the broken links
preview: RN-04 has no test — broken link

sdd-setup.when: First time in the project, or the stack changed
sdd-setup.generates: config.yml, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, permissions and a stack report

spike.when: Estimate a card before taking it
spike.generates: The parts of the work with the hours you decide
preview: AI suggestion: 3 h + 5 h + 2 h = 10 h
You decide: 12 h — only your value is saved

code-review.when: Review a branch or PR outside the plan
code-review.generates: CR-XX report with severity and Q1–Q4 quadrant
preview: CR-01 Bloqueante · Q1 — fix before merge

architecture.intro: The kit is a set of files your AI reads; the result lives in your repository. Activate a block to see its links, or follow the path of one command.

panel.hint: Activate a block in the diagram — click, tap or Enter — to see what it does, its files and its command.

flow.title: The path of /sdd-prd
steps: It reads the ID conventions from templates
It reads the project stack profile
The PRD is saved in docs/sdd/prds/

skills.title: Skills
skills.text: Each command is a skill: a SKILL.md with the procedure and a references/ folder with templates. The same file works in Claude Code and Codex.

templates.title: Templates
templates.text: Rules every skill shares: ID formats, where each document lives and how to read a Jira, GitHub or plain-text card.

stacks.title: Stacks
stacks.text: One profile per stack with versions, commands, tests and a security checklist. Rails is the complete profile; Node, Python, .NET, Go, Java and PHP have light profiles; anything else uses the generic one.

adapters.title: Adapters
adapters.text: How each AI receives the kit. Claude Code uses the repository as a plugin; Codex gets the skills through an installer.

claude.title: Claude Code
claude.text: The reference AI: skills become slash commands and project permissions live in .claude/settings.json.

codex.title: Codex
codex.text: Gets the same skills in .agents/skills/ and calls them with a dollar sign. Shared file paths are adjusted at install time.

others.title: Other AIs
others.text: No adapter yet. The contract says where a new AI keeps skills, the context file, permissions and arguments.

agents.title: AGENTS.md
agents.text: The file every AI reads first: stack, commands, conventions and where the pipeline documents are. Written by /sdd-setup.

claudemd.title: CLAUDE.md
claudemd.text: Just points to AGENTS.md and adds what is specific to Claude Code.

config.title: docs/sdd/config.yml
config.text: The kit configuration for the project: stacks and versions, test commands, document language, AIs in use and base branch.

docs.title: docs/sdd/
docs.text: Everything the phases produce: architecture and ADRs, PRDs, SPEC-UI, plans, reviews and traceability matrices — versioned with the code.

stacks.intro: /sdd-setup reads the project’s real versions and loads the stack profile. Rails is the complete reference; the others have light profiles, and anything without a profile uses the generic one. The AI can change: the context lives in a single file.
stacks.stacksLabel: Stacks with a profile in the kit
stacks.hubLabel: AGENTS.md linked to the coding AIs
stacks.hubNote: Supported means the skills run as commands. In other AIs, AGENTS.md already provides the context; a dedicated adapter can come through the adapters/ contract.

openSource.intro: Open source under the MIT license. Use it, adapt it and contribute — the kit is designed to grow through stack profiles and adapters.

contribute.text: Open an issue with a bug, question or idea
Bring the kit to another AI
Every change goes through the CI check

openSource.license: MIT: free use, including commercial, as long as the copyright notice is kept.
openSource.madeTitle: This site was built with MyAiToolKit
openSource.madeText: The architecture, ADRs, PRD, SPEC-UI, plan, one review per task and the traceability matrix of this page are versioned in the site repository.

install.intro: Clone the kit repository and install it in your AI. The commands are the same as in the kit README.

claude.check: After installing, run /plugin inside Claude Code to check that the 12 skills were loaded.

codex.note: Skills go to ~/.agents/skills/. With --scope repo, they live in the project’s .agents/skills/, versioned with it.

others.text: Content is written once, in the portable skill format, and each AI gets an adapter. Until an adapter exists, the AI can already read the AGENTS.md that /sdd-setup writes.
others.nextNote: Not supported yet — contributions are welcome.

install.firstUseText: Inside your project: /sdd-setup writes the configuration and AGENTS.md; /sdd-start asks where the demand begins.

code.claudeInstall:
git clone https://github.com/fbzsaullo/MyAiToolKit.git MyAiToolKit
claude plugin marketplace add ./MyAiToolKit
claude plugin install my-ai-toolkit@my-ai-toolkit
